thread.title: Dow set to lead Wall Street higher on signs of thawing trade tensions - MarketWatch

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Dow set to lead Wall Street higher on signs of thawing trade tensions - MarketWatch
text:
U.S. stocks rallied midday Wednesday as gains by banks and the tech sector helped to extend an advance for the broader market.
Read: Here’s why Italy and financial markets are still headed for a showdown
What are the markets doing? The Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.40% rose 226 points, or 0.9%, to 25,028, while the S&P 500 SPX, +0.86% added 11 points, or less than 0.4%, at 2,760, while the Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +0.67% rose 15 points, or 0.2%, at 7,653.
The small cap-oriented Russell 2000 index RUT, +0.68% which has outperformed its larger peers, extended its march higher, up 0.2% at 1,668.
On Tuesday , the Dow finished down less than 0.1% at 24,799.98, while the S&P 500 index rose less than 0.1% to 2,748.79. The Nasdaq advanced 0.4% to 7,637.86, marking a second record close and the third consecutive advance for the tech-laden equity gauge.
Also read: First-half volatility sets stage for stock market’s ‘next leg higher,’ says prominent bull
What is driving the market? An advance for financials, notably shares of JPMorgan Chase & Co . JPM, +2.34% up 2.1% and Goldman Sachs Group Inc. GS, +1.70% rising by 1.1%, were boosted in part by a rise in the yield of the benchmark 10-year Treasury note TMUBMUSD10Y, +1.69% The yield rose to 2.97% Wednesday from 2.917% late Tuesday in New York. Yields rise as bond prices fall and climbing rates are generally bullish for banks’ business models.
Investors were also on alert for developments on the trade front, with Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin reportedly urging President Donald Trump to exempt Canada from metals tariffs at a meeting Tuesday. That adds to a report Wednesday that China had offered to buy some $70 billion of U.S. goods to get the Trump administration to cool its tariff threats .
Tensions are still simmering, however, after Mexico revealed which U.S. products it is targeting for import tariffs —around $3 billion for goods including apples and bourbon—in retaliation for U.S. duties on Mexican steel and aluminum.
Leaders of the Group of Seven nations will likely discuss trade as they hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday. Tension between the U.S. and the six other members is expected, given the hostile reactions to tariffs imposed by the Trump administration.
Overall, gains for technology stocks have been driven by the belief among some that sector heavyweights such as Netflix Inc . NFLX, +0.45% and Apple Inc . AAPL, +0.35% could weather an economic pullback, if that happens.
Meanwhile, some market observers were worried that investor complacency may be setting in, after the Cboe Volatility Index VIX, -6.05% hit its lowest level since late January on Tuesday, falling 2.7% to 12.40. On Wednesday, the VIX was at 12.09, off more than 2% and down nearly 10% in the first three sessions of the week.
What are strategists saying? “Generally, we are still in a bull market in a day where we have no bad news, we’re going to see the market drift higher,” said Randy Frederick, managing director of trading and derivatives at Schwab Center for Financial Research.
“If the market can stay on the trend that it’s been on, we should be hitting a new high in September,” he speculated, referring to highs for the S&P 500 index and the Dow, which have lagged behind the Nasdaq’s recent record run.
See: First-half volatility sets stage for stock market’s ‘next leg higher,’ says prominent bull
What’s on the economic calendar? The U.S. trade deficit shrank 2.1% in April —before the Trump tariffs took effect—and tumbled to a seven-month low. But the gap is still on track to widen in 2018 to the highest level in a decade.
Meanwhile, the productivity of American businesses rose at a revised 0.4% annual pace in the first quarter instead of 0.7% as originally reported. Output—or goods and services produced—climbed 2.7% instead of 2.8%, while unit-labor costs, or how much it costs to make each product, rose by 2.9%, a bit higher than the preliminary 2.7% estimate, the government said Wednesday.

Which stocks are in focus? Tesla Inc . TSLA, +9.74% shares rose 7% after Chief Executive Elon Musk told shareholders that the electric-car maker was “quite likely” to meet its production goal of 5,000 Model 3 cars a week.
Read : Tesla investors missed opportunity to hold Elon Musk & Co. accountable
Also : Latest Wall Street view on Tesla is a cautious one
UnitedHealth Group Inc. UNH, +1.73% shares rose 1% after the health-care company raised its quarterly dividend by 20% .
Facebook Inc. FB, -0.83% shares fell 1.4% after the social-media giant confirmed it had shared user data with at least four Chinese tech companies . U.S. officials have warned that devices from one of those companies — Huawei Technologies Co.— could be exploited for state-sponsored spying.
Twitter Inc. TWTR, +0.75% shares fell 0.1% after announcing plans for an $1 billion convertible debt offering.
Signet Jewelers Ltd . shares SIG, +18.39% surged more than 22% after the company beat estimates for its fiscal first quarter to May 5.
Shares of Axovant Sciences Ltd . AXON, +160.00% soared nearly 121%, after Oxford BioMedica PLC OXB, +18.92% said it has entered an $842.5 million licensing agreement for OXB-102, a gene therapy treatment for Parkinson’s disease.
Athenahealth Inc . ATHN, +4.17% said Wednesday it has begun exploring “strategic alternatives,” in which the hospital and ambulatory-services company will consider a sale, merger or other transaction. Shares of the company rose 4.1%.
